description: Replace the free-text multi-Bot ambiguity prompt with one Server-signed interactive Slack chooser per ambiguous message, whose accepted selection starts exactly one execution for the chosen Connection from the original message, with durable decision authority, restart recovery, and bounded cleanup.

tasks.title: Extract the channel-root launch core into SlackChannelLaunchService
tasks.description: Behavior-preserving preparatory refactor (design Decision 6): extract the core of the private LaunchChannelRootAsync in SlackConnectionRoutes.ChannelIngress.cs into an internal SlackChannelLaunchService parameterized by connection, message identity, sender, text, files, thread anchor, and pre-minted launch ids, so channel ingress and the later selection dispatch invoke the identical launch sequence (thread launch reservation, provider inbox route, attachment binder, InteractionWorkspaceProvisioner, admission, LaunchConnectionAsync with ConnectionLaunchOrigin). All existing channel ingress call sites switch to the extracted service with unchanged outcomes.
acceptanceCriteria: The thread launch reservation, provider inbox route, attachment binding, admission, and LaunchConnectionAsync sequence run through SlackChannelLaunchService for every existing channel-root ingress call site in SlackConnectionRoutes.ChannelIngress.cs.
PreMintSlackLaunchIds deterministic identity derivation is reachable from the service without a delivering-Connection request context (parameterized inputs only).
No observable ingress behavior changes: existing SlackChannelThreadIngressSpecs, SlackMultiAgentIngressSpecs, SlackChannelThreadReplySpecs, and SlackChannelAdmissionNudgeSpecs pass unchanged.
No duplicate launch logic remains private to the route partial for the channel-root path; the provider inbox still owns only raw Slack message ingress.
Relevant Server tests and the fast Server test suite pass.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Slack/Services/SlackChannelLaunchService.cs with ingress call sites switched over, plus green existing channel ingress spec suites.
tasks.notes: Guarded by existing spec coverage; the extraction must not alter admission or nudge outcomes. Design risk entry 'Extracting the launch core risks regressing the ingress path' is covered by requiring existing specs to stay green.

tasks.title: Interactive chooser claim with durable original-message facts
tasks.description: Deliver the slack-agent-selection-prompt capability (design Decisions 1-3): extend SlackAmbiguousPromptRow/SlackAmbiguousPromptStore with non-nullable retained input facts (original sender, task text with all mentioned workspace-Bot tokens removed via a multi-mention RemoveBotMention variant, FilesJson, thread anchor) and selection-state columns (SelectionState, ChosenConnectionId, pre-allocated identity slots, worker bookkeeping, FinishedAt/SettleReason) written by the same once-only INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING claim, with one additive EF migration including the (ProjectId, SelectionState, UpdatedAt) worker scan index. Replace the plain-text ambiguity prompt in HandleAmbiguousPromptAsync with one actions block of buttons sharing action id mohist_select_agent, one per mentioned workspace Bot, each carrying a SlackSelectionActionPayload (version, action, posting Connection, team/conversation/original message ts, thread ts, actor, ordered candidate set, chosen candidate, nonce, 24h expiry) signed with ISlackActionSigner over the Stop/Retry canonical form, delivered through the winner's outbox UserAction delivery under the existing stable dispatch reference with a plain-text fallback. The non-owner path (HandleAmbiguousNonOwnerAsync) and SlackMultiAgentRoutingPolicy stay unchanged, and the ambiguous message itself creates no AgentJob, AgentSession, SessionInput, or provider inbox entry.
acceptanceCriteria: A root multi-Bot mention posts exactly one chooser at the channel root and an ambiguous multi-bound-thread reply posts exactly one chooser in that thread, each with one button per mentioned workspace Bot and no plain-text 'mention a single Bot' prompt; unambiguous messages render no chooser.

Concurrent per-Connection ingress, Slack event redelivery, and adapter failover collapse to one chooser via the once-only claim; a loser posts nothing; only the winner may retry an unpersisted delivery under the stable dispatch reference and a caller observing an existing delivery enqueues nothing.

Candidate choices are exactly parsed mentions intersected with workspace identity-bound Bots, deduplicated by Bot user id; human mentions and other-Servers' Bots never appear; duplicate Bot identities collapse to one choice without added ambiguity.

The claim durably retains sender identity, mention-stripped task text, attachment metadata, and thread anchor in non-nullable columns: store unit tests prove a claim cannot exist without facts and facts survive to lookup; a claim lacking facts can start no execution (surfaced, never reconstructed).

Each button value is a structurally valid signed payload whose constant-time HMAC verification succeeds for the posting Connection and fails for tampered fields or another Connection's key; expiry is fixed at render time.
No AgentJob, AgentSession, SessionInput, or provider inbox entry is created for any ambiguous message at ingress (both root multi-mention and multi-bound-thread reply scenarios).
The unauthorized-sender path still posts the existing owner-only guidance once, unchanged, with no chooser and no work.

Fixed-time fake-port spec tests cover the chooser scenarios (root, thread, unambiguous, fan-out, redelivery, winner retry, candidates, non-owner, no-resources) and the EF migration applies additively with existing pre-fact rows requiring no backfill.
tasks.output: Extended SlackAmbiguousPromptStore/SlackAmbiguousPromptRow with a new EF migration, SlackSelectionActionPayload with render-time signing, chooser block rendering in SlackConnectionRoutes.ChannelIngress.cs, and prompt-capability spec/unit tests.
tasks.notes: Design Decision 2 mandates buttons over static_select so the Go adapter contract stays untouched. Decision 1 keeps one durable record (no second selection-operations table). Expiry default 24h pending the Open Questions confirmation.

tasks.title: Signed selection action handling with single-execution dispatch
tasks.description: Deliver the slack-agent-selection-action capability and the live-path core of slack-selection-execution-attribution (design Decisions 3-6, 8): add SlackAgentSelectionService.HandleAsync beside the Stop/Retry services, dispatched from SlackInteractionRoutes by action id mohist_select_agent with lease context while reusing unchanged operator authentication, runtime lease validation (stale lease -> lease_stale_or_expired before any processing), disabled-Connection check, and outbox UserAction reply delivery with ActionDispatchRef idempotency. The fixed-order acceptance pipeline: signature/structure (invalid_action), freshness (expired), context including the durable chooser-message identity resolved from the acked outbox ProviderMessageIdentity (stale_action), actor binding to the original sender only (unauthorized), recorded-decision short-circuit returning the decision view, candidate validity (no_longer_valid), clicker permission re-evaluated via SlackConnectionAccessDecider under the chosen Connection's current policy with the interaction lease context, and executability via the existing SlackAdmissionService setup-nudge / connection_disabled outcomes. Commit is a single compare-and-swap on the claim row to SelectionState Decided with pre-allocated deterministic ids (PreMintSlackLaunchIds derivation over the original message identity), then dispatch: root multi-mention launches through SlackChannelLaunchService with the original sender and message identity as provenance; an ambiguous multi-bound-thread reply dispatches a follow-up via RouteFollowupAsync to the chosen Connection's currently bound session (missing binding -> no_longer_valid, never a new Session); loser Connections remain no-ops. Rejections are distinct visible notices updating the chooser message and create no execution resources. The Go adapter gains only test coverage for the new action id.
acceptanceCriteria: The interaction route dispatches mohist_select_agent to SlackAgentSelectionService with the same authentication and lease validation as Stop and Retry; a stale lease returns lease_stale_or_expired before any selection processing; Stop and Retry outcomes are unchanged by coexistence.

Each rejection kind (tampered/foreign-key invalid, expired, context or chooser-message mismatch stale, wrong actor or currently-disallowed clicker unauthorized with the policy's actionable reason, vanished candidate or binding no_longer_valid) produces a distinct visible notice updating the chooser message and creates no AgentJob, AgentSession, SessionInput, selection mutation, or provider inbox entry; agent-not-ready posts the existing setup nudge durably and a disabled chosen Connection returns the existing connection-disabled outcome.
A click on a stale duplicate chooser (outbox delivery retry) or a copied value, and a click on a delivered-but-unacked chooser, are rejected as stale with no resources.

An accepted root-mention selection launches the chosen Connection's Session in that thread from the retained facts with the original sender as initiator and the original message identity as provenance, attachments bound via the existing binder, entering the provider inbox through the launch route; an accepted thread-reply selection dispatches a follow-up to the chosen Connection's bound session creating no new Session.

Concurrent clicks on the same or different candidates, repeated clicks, interaction redelivery, adapter failover, and lost interaction responses resolve to exactly one recorded selection (CAS) and at most one AgentJob/Session/SessionInput lineage attributed to the chosen Connection; every loser or late clicker observes the decision view, never a second chooser or execution.

The decision is durably persisted with pre-allocated execution identity before any dispatch, and no dispatch path may start work for the message outside that record (crash between commit and dispatch leaves the authority intact).
The same launch and admission services the CLI/Web use are invoked (no Slack-only execution path), and no other mentioned or bound Connection creates any execution resource for the message.

Fake-port fixed-time spec tests cover the full acceptance matrix, the concurrency/redelivery/lost-response attribution scenarios, and provenance; Go adapter tests cover block_actions forwarding of the selection action id with no adapter contract change.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Slack/Services/SlackAgentSelectionService.cs, three-way action-id dispatch in SlackInteractionRoutes, CAS commit in SlackAmbiguousPromptStore, launch/follow-up dispatch wiring, selection spec tests, and Go adapter test coverage for the new action id.
tasks.notes: Also satisfies the live-path requirements of specs/slack-selection-execution-attribution/spec.md (start-from-original-message, exactly-one-execution, durable-decision-before-dispatch, at-most-one-under-concurrency). Render-time authorization is never trusted; the Owner clicking another member's chooser is unauthorized per the strict actor rule.

tasks.title: Selection obligation worker: recovery, expiry settlement, retention, and docs
tasks.description: Deliver restart recovery and bounded cleanup (design Decision 7): a SlackAgentSelectionObligationWorker mirroring SlackAgentAppBindingObligationWorker that periodically resumes Decided rows whose dispatch has not completed by re-running the idempotent launch/follow-up dispatch under the pre-allocated identity, terminally settles committed selections that can no longer produce their execution (Settled with reason plus one visible outbox UserAction outcome under a stable dispatch reference, nothing executing afterwards), expires Pending rows past expiry plus a grace margin as expired, and reaps Completed/Settled rows older than the retention bound (default 7 days) while never removing pending or in-progress operations. Update docs/slack.md and design/slack.md to move multi-Bot selection from planned to delivered.
acceptanceCriteria: A restart between commit and dispatch resumes the selection to completion using the pre-allocated execution identity, producing the recorded execution exactly once and never a duplicate (fake-port recovery specs).

An unrecoverable committed selection (chosen Connection or Agent gone, lineage irrecoverable after repeated failures) is settled terminally with a visible outcome and creates no execution resources after settlement.
A Pending row past expiry plus grace is settled expired, and a late click on it is still rejected as expired by the freshness check regardless of the sweep.
Cleanup removes only Completed/Settled records older than the retention bound; pending and in-progress records are never reaped (spec scenario coverage).
The worker scans via the (ProjectId, SelectionState, UpdatedAt) index with bounded retry intervals and failure logging per the obligation-worker pattern; repeated resume attempts remain idempotent.
docs/slack.md and design/slack.md Status/gap notes present multi-Bot interactive selection as delivered, including the chooser and single-execution attribution behavior.
Recovery and retention spec tests plus the full Server fast test suite pass.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Slack/Services/SlackAgentSelectionObligationWorker.cs with DI registration, recovery/expiry/retention spec tests, and updated docs/slack.md plus design/slack.md status notes.
tasks.notes: Retention default 7d and pending-settlement grace 24h past expiry per design Open Questions; confirm bounds against Slack delayed-event windows during implementation.
